key_insight: AA-ViT uses anatomical, structural, and frequency guidance in a vision transformer to synthesize contrast-enhanced brain MRI that better preserves tumour and tissue boundaries.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this could help reduce reliance on gadolinium contrast, shorten scan workflows, and improve access to lesion-enhancing MRI when contrast use is unsuitable.
method: Uses pre-contrast MRI inputs: T1, T2, and FLAIR
Combines anatomical awareness with structural and frequency guidance
Applies a vision transformer to generate synthetic post-contrast scans
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2021, the model outperformed state-of-the-art methods on PSNR and SSIM, and three neuroradiologists plus a neurosurgeon gave a mean clinical score of 3.94/5 across 19 cases.
watch_item: Results are promising but based on limited clinical evaluation, so broader external validation and real-world testing are needed before routine use.
paper_title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis
